papers.one_line: The authors demonstrate a physically executed static-arena pipeline with Vicon localization checks and shorter reported times on two layouts. Strict evidence-level rules require counted physical successes/trials for online or transfer; those denominators are absent.

Author-reported controlled teacher-variant gains in closed-loop OWMM and unchanged OWMM-policy success on counted AI2-THOR navigation episodes support training utility and limited cross-simulator transfer. Physical deployment's 38% lacks local textual trial totals; broad open-world robustness is not established.

Author-reported matched-backbone VLN gains for the goal/verification bundle, memory token savings with explicit quality losses, and counted Go2 deployment support scoped sim-to-physical transfer. No independent reproduction, isolated verifier effect, calibrated checker reliability or universal efficiency dominance established.

Author-reported counted LIBERO closed-loop results support compatible topology-preserving inference variations; qualitative simulation/FR3 cases demonstrate orchestration feasibility. They do not measure engineering savings, safe lifecycle reliability or end-to-end LLM-agent success, and uncounted hardware cases do not qualify as transfer.

Authors report counted closed-loop simulation EQA improvements on filtered prior-available subsets across five backbones, with informative one-component and same-prior controls. Qualitative physical examples and offline replay do not establish counted transfer, calibrated stopping, full-benchmark SOTA or robustness to erroneous floorplans.

Authors report useful fixed-navigator predictor/backtracking controls and counted Turtlebot4 transfer on25instructions, with a3success advantage for backtracking. This supports modest taskset-specific recovery gains and improved waypoint quality, not training-free entire system, blanket metric dominance, general dynamic safety or parity with strong supervised simulation methods.
